I didn't write the FAP, because a stock Flipper on official firmware 1.5.1 can't do what the request needs. The kettle is a BLE peripheral, so the Flipper would have to scan, connect and read or write as a BLE central. The pinned 1.5.1 SDK (API 88.2) configures the radio as a peripheral only and doesn't export any central or GATT-client calls. That means a FAP would call functions that don't exist. This comes from the research notes in the repo's Flipper skill. I haven't built or run anything on a device.

My recommended route is a Flipper FAP for the UI plus a small BLE-capable companion board, such as an ESP32, linked over UART. The board does the BLE work, including the 30-second idle reconnects. It would need to be checked for BLE central support and 3.3 V compatibility first. A computer or Raspberry Pi would also work, but it conflicts with "no phone needed" only if you count it as the same thing.

`kettle-protocol.md` doesn't say how the checksum is calculated, what the status frames look like, or what value turns the kettle on or off. Those need capture evidence before any code is written.

I'm waiting on your choice of route. Once you pick one, I can write the FAP and the UART protocol spec, plus either the board firmware or a host script.

The full feasibility card is in `/tmp/fred-eval/pilot2/9bc59a1c1e/ws/compatibility-card.md`.
